about: The tokens of Promenade's design system: the one source of colour, type, spacing, radii, elevation, motion and sizes. Everything else that shows them is generated from this file by design/tools/build-system.mjs (tokens.css, the map styles) or reads it (the system's page, the checks). A colour is #rrggbb or #rrggbbaa. A length is a number of points: px on the web, pt on iOS, dp on Android.

color.about: Three themes. Light is the daytime default and dark is a choice. Sun is for bright sunlight: every pane is solid, text is held to 7 : 1, lines are heavier. A name is a role, never a hue.

roles.surface: The solid page: what the guide says is read on it. Also what a pane of glass becomes when it is solid.
roles.surface-2: A well on the page: a field, a tile, a pressed row.
roles.ink-2: Second ink: a label, a value, a sentence not being spoken.
roles.ink-3: Graphics only, never text: a grabber, an outline, the walked part of the line.
roles.rule: A hairline between two parts of a pane.
roles.accent: The fill of “on time”: the one prominent action, the current stop, the person. It always carries on-accent content or stands beside words.
roles.on-accent: Text and icons on the accent.
roles.accent-ink: “On time” as text, a link, a footnote mark.
roles.line: The Route on the map and every graphic that carries “on time” without words beside it.
roles.line-case: The casing that lifts the line off the map.
roles.warn: A warning, as text and as a graphic.
roles.on-warn: Text on the fill of a warning.
roles.stop: A broken constraint, an error, a destructive action, as text and as a graphic.
roles.stop-fill: The fill of an error or of a destructive action.
roles.on-stop: Text on the fill of an error.
roles.ok-tint: The ground of a verdict “on time”, laid over a pane.
roles.warn-tint: The ground of a warning, laid over a pane.
roles.stop-tint: The ground of an error, laid over a pane.
roles.scrim: What dims the screen behind a dialog.
roles.photo-scrim: The ground of a credit laid over a photograph.
roles.photo-min: The darkest a photograph can be under a pane: used only to measure contrast.
roles.photo-max: The lightest a photograph can be under a pane: used only to measure contrast.
roles.marker: The disc of a stop on the map.
roles.mark: The capsule of a clock time written on the line.
roles.m-street: Map: a street, and the halo of a street name.
roles.m-street-edge: Map: the edge of a street; drawn only where it differs from the ground.
roles.m-building: Map: a building seen from above.
roles.m-roof: Map: the roof of a standing building.
roles.m-wall: Map: its walls, and the outline of a roof.
roles.m-place: Map: the footprint of a Place of the Route, laid over its building.
roles.haze: Map: what distance dissolves into when the map is seen at an angle.
roles.lg-fill: Liquid Glass, regular: a sheet, a bar, a card of controls. May carry text.
roles.lg-fill-clear: Liquid Glass, clear: a small control over the map. Icons and short labels only, never over a photograph.
roles.lg-edge: The bright edge of a pane, where the light comes from.
roles.lg-edge-low: The same edge, away from the light.
roles.md-surface: Android: a Material surface in place of regular glass.
roles.md-surface-high: Android: a Material surface in place of clear glass, and a card on a surface.

contrast.about: Every pair of a text or a graphic and the ground it stands on, checked by `pnpm lint:design` against WCAG 2.2 level AA: 4.5 : 1 for text, 3 : 1 for large text and for graphics. In the sun theme text is held to 7 : 1 and large text to 4.5 : 1, which is this system's own rule. A ground written as { over, each } is a translucent token laid over each of the listed tokens: the worst of them counts. Text on glass is measured over every area the map can put under a pane; a line of the map is narrower than the blur of the glass and is left out.

pairs.use: Ink on regular glass over a photograph, at its lightest and its darkest
Android: second ink on a surface
Android: ink on a raised surface
Android: second ink on a raised surface
Android: “on time” on a raised surface
A clock time on the line
A street name on its halo
A name on the ground of the map
The line on the ground of the map
The spine, the rule, a lamp on the page
A grabber, an outline, the walked line
The walked line on the map

font.about: Three faces, one for each kind of saying, all under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 and all carrying Cyrillic and the Belarusian letters ў and ŭ. The map's names are set in the face whose glyph ranges ship with the map (ADR-0008).

text.use: What the timetable says in words

type.about: The type scale. size and line are points; tracking is in em. scales says whether the role grows with the system's text size: “full” up to 200 %, “capped” up to 130 % because it is already large, “none” for a numeral that is part of a graphic and has a text alternative.

clock-xl.use: The two times of the Outing, on a wide screen

clock-l.use: The two times of the Outing

clock-m.use: A time that leads a pane: the lock screen, a dialog

numeral.use: The number of a stop in its disc

wordmark.use: The name of the product in a bar

title-l.use: The title of a pane on a wide screen

action.use: The label of the prominent action

row.use: The name of a Place in a row

body.use: What the timetable says at length; a field

body-strong.use: A clock time in a row; the label of a second action

label.use: A verdict, a status, a fact

label-strong.use: The word that leads a verdict

caption.use: A unit, a leg of the walk, the label over a time

micro.use: A credit, the attribution of the map: the smallest text there is

tab.use: The name of a destination in the bar: it stops at 130 %, and the system shows it large on a long press

guide-title-l.use: The name of a Place on the guide's page, wide or opened in full

guide-title.use: The name of a Place on the guide's page

guide-body-l.use: The Story, wide or opened in full

guide-aside.use: Why a Place is on the Route

guide-note.use: The source of a Story, at the foot of the page

space.about: Distances. A name is its value, so nothing has to be looked up.

radius.about: Corners. iOS follows the concentric, capsule shapes of Liquid Glass; Android follows the shape scale of Material 3 Expressive. A value written once is the same on both.

m.use: A verdict, a note, a banner

photo.use: The photograph at the head of a page

card.use: The capsule of the player, a card of controls

sheet.use: A sheet: floating with all corners on iOS, attached with the top corners on Android

size.about: Sizes held by rule. target is the least size of anything that can be touched, checked by `pnpm lint:design` and on the system's check page.

target.use: Apple asks for 44 pt, Android for 48 dp; both clear the 24 px of WCAG 2.2 criterion 2.5.8

control.use: A round control, a field, a row of a list

action.use: The prominent action and what stands beside it

icon-s.use: An icon beside a line of text

icon-stroke.use: The weight of an icon's line on a 24 grid

sheet-inset.use: How far a sheet stands from the edges of the screen

reach.use: The share of the screen's height, from the bottom, that a thumb reaches with one hand: what is used on the move stays inside it

elevation.about: How a pane leaves the ground. On iOS and the web, glass is lifted by a soft shadow and a bright edge; on Android a surface takes the shadow of its Material level. Written as CSS box shadows, which React Native reads as well.

blur.use: The blur behind a pane of glass, in points. Zero in the sun theme, on Android, in the saver mode and with “reduce transparency”.

motion.about: How long a thing takes and how it moves. Durations are milliseconds. A spring is given as the application will use it; the CSS easing is computed from the same three numbers. With “reduce motion” set, movement becomes a cross-fade of `fade` and nothing loops.

fade.use: A cross-fade; the whole of a change under “reduce motion”

move.use: A pane changes its size or place

follow.use: The rule glides to the sentence being spoken

arrive.use: The map tilts and the guide's page rises on arrival

redraw.use: The line is drawn along a new course

roll.use: A clock time rolls to its new value

march.use: One period of the dashes of the way ahead

voice.use: One beat of the bar under the playhead

breath.use: One breath of the mark of the person

standard.use: Most movement: quick to leave, slow to settle

enter.use: What comes in from an edge

linear.use: What tracks time itself: the playhead, the march

glass.use: A pane of glass that grows, joins or follows a finger

page.use: The guide's page as it rises: no overshoot

sound.about: Two short sounds, designed with the motion. Each is a few plain tones with a soft attack, made by the device itself, so there is no file and no licence. They are quieter than a Story and never play over speech; with the phone on silent only the touch remains. Frequencies are hertz, times milliseconds.

arrival.use: On arrival, with the ring that leaves the Place: two notes, the second a fifth above the first

story.use: A breath before the first word of a Story that starts by itself

map.about: What the style of the map needs beyond colour: the widths of streets by zoom and the camera of the two views. design/tools/build-system.mjs writes the MapLibre styles from these and from the colours.

plan.use: The Route before the start: seen from above, north up

walk.use: The Outing: seen at an angle, the direction of travel up, buildings standing

saver.use: The Outing in the saver mode: flat, heading up, nothing extruded, no blur, nothing in motion

line.use: The line of the Route, in points

buildings.use: Standing buildings on the way: lower than life, so that the line and the Place ahead stay in sight

streets.about: Width in points at zoom 13, 15 and 17.
